input.body:
label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts

The parser splits the file only on `"
"` (line 72), so it doesn't account for Windows-style CRLF line endings. Since finance's new accounting export tool runs on Windows and likely produces `
` line endings, each line (including the header) ends up with a trailing `` character, which throws off the column count/comparison and triggers the "errors.rowShape" ("Malformed row") error on the very first row. The parser should normalize line endings (e.g. strip `` or split on `/
|
/`) before processing rows.

text: This confirms it — the parser splits on `"\n"` only, so Windows CRLF line endings (from the new Windows export tool) leave a trailing `\r` on each field, causing column counts/content mismatches, which triggers the "Malformed row" error on row 1.
